# Comprehensive Project Audit — 2026-06-03

*Two-pass (knowledge-ful audit + independent knowledge-free verification), 11 slices, 23 reviewers. Generated by the project-audit workflow.*

## Headline

Docs are mostly healthy historical archive; the only HIGH-severity, both-agree fixes are two production-path docs that contradict live code: the engine-wiring spec still says "no implementation yet" when the full-pool sampler IS the production default, and PRODUCT_GUIDE.md + README.md still claim the project is mid-Phase-2 ("9 of 11 engines", "API/frontend unbuilt") with README citing two nonexistent install scripts. backlog.xlsx has drifted badly from BACKLOG.md (SIM-043 catcher engine and ~40 closed Phase-4 tickets still "Open", broken Dashboard formulas, misnamed Phase 7 sheet) and has NO generator script — RETIRE it (or build a generator first). Code is in good shape: no correctness bugs, only dead-wiring (SIM-321 ScoreFusion never runs in production; metrics counters/freshness gauge silently read 0/-1) and stale comments. Also: CLAUDE.md itself now says DuckDB schema "v11" when actual is v13.

## Agreement summary (audit vs independent verify)

Very high agreement across all 11 slices. Verify broadly AGREED with every audit pass and confirmed the load-bearing claims independently against live code, git history, and config. No verify pass overturned an audit's overall verdict; disagreements were narrow scope refinements or factual corrections, never reversals.

DISPUTED (1, narrowed not reversed): similarity_calibration.py finding #5 — both agree on the 4 duplicated _zscore closures, but verify disputed the audit's claim that all four older calibrators feed calibrate_sigma directly (the spurious sigma=1.0 risk). Fielder and baserunner already route through _fit_sigma per SIM-432; the real latent risk is only batter + pitcher. Action scoped accordingly.

AUDIT-ONLY / verify-corrected-the-audit (1): scripts/backfill_odds_hash.py — the audit called it 'idempotent and dependency-correct', but verify found its dedup DELETE orders by a non-existent column 'received_at' (actual: fetched_at), so that branch would raise against the real schema. Contradicts the audit's correctness label; impact nil (dead one-shot).

Notable items verify ADDED that the audit missed (all fold into both-agree actions): (1) CLAUDE.md itself states DuckDB schema 'v11' in 3 live places when actual is v13 — a concrete factual error in the canonical reference, not just a stale TL;DR date; (2) the metrics baseball_sim_api_p95_seconds docstring is stale in the OPPOSITE direction (a now-live SIM-410-fed series labeled PLACEHOLDER); (3) .gitignore has no '~$*' pattern and xlsx_fullbacklog.json is an unignored stray; (4) sim_loop.py:3792 machine.pitcher_rest_days getattr is always-None dead-wiring (production_factory never stages it, unlike machine.bullpen); (5) two live_ingestion_pipeline route handlers also bypass the odds provider seam (same family as the opening_line_job finding, lower impact); (6) the SIM-411/413/425b/427 roadmap 'plans' were fully EXECUTED (migrations 0012/0013), more superseded than the audit framed.

Cross-cutting theme both passes surfaced: slice headers consistently miscounted files (claimed 22 SPRINT logs / 11 ADRs / 14 audits; actual 19 / 10 / 13) — coverage was complete, only the framing counts were off. The dominant doc disposition is keep-as-archive (faithful point-in-time records with expected snapshot drift); the genuine fixes concentrate in a handful of live-facing docs (PRODUCT_GUIDE, README, WORKFLOW, the engine-wiring spec, the two ACTIVE-labeled perf budgets, CLAUDE.md's v11) and dead-wiring code (ScoreFusion, metrics counters/freshness, opening_line_job odds seam, require_api_key). No correctness bugs in any production code path.

## backlog.xlsx findings

backlog.xlsx has drifted SEVERELY from BACKLOG.md (the authoritative tracker) and BOTH passes agree. The drift is systematic, not isolated:

SIM-043 (the user's flagged example): the catcher-similarity engine shows status 'Open' in the Full Backlog sheet, but it demonstrably shipped in Phase 2 — similarity/engines/catcher_similarity.py is a real 768-line registered engine (SIM-072 v2), Phase 2 CLOSED 2026-05-20, and the live app logs build_all_engines: 11/11. It is a canary for the broader drift.

Scope of drift (verify re-tallied: 102 non-closed rows, not the audit's 95): the ENTIRE Phase-4 tier (SIM-220 + SIM-310..349, 41 rows) shows 'Open' though BACKLOG.md declares 'PHASE 4 COMPLETE' — 40 of those should be Closed (SIM-315 is correctly Closed). The six/seven audit live-bugs (SIM-312/313/322/336/337/345/346) all show 'Open' though all are fixed. Dozens of Phase-2/3 rows are stale (SIM-107 'done via SIM-348', SIM-120 'unblocked by SIM-320', SIM-160/161 'Shipped 2026-05-20' all still Open). Recent tickets lag (SIM-430 'Open' despite worker-scaling RESOLVED; SIM-433/434/435 'Code-complete' missing the 2026-06-03 v2 ingest). Newest IDs are entirely missing (no SIM-425b, no SIM-437; SIM-403b appended out of order at row 224). Confirmed via the untracked xlsx_fullbacklog.json export.

Structural defects: the Dashboard status/priority counters are COUNTIF formulas with NO cached values (workbook never recalculated in Excel, so counts render blank), AND they match only the literal strings Closed/Open/Held/In Progress while 12 rows use verbose statuses ('Shipped 2026-05-14...', 'Code-complete', 'Open – Sprint 2026-05-20') that no COUNTIF will ever match — so even after recalc the totals under-count and Total != 238. The 'Phase 7 Gate' sheet contains old Phase-2-era tickets (SIM-130..158) and NONE of the real Phase 7 work (SIM-402/406/407/408/430/431/432/433/434/435/436) — its name no longer matches its contents. 'Current Sprint' carries three contradictory dates (banner 2026-06-01, Dashboard 2026-06-10, body = Phase-3 circa 2026-05). Same IDs appear in multiple sheets with divergent statuses (internal inconsistency).

Root cause (verify's decisive finding): NO generator script exists anywhere in the repo — no .py imports openpyxl or references 'backlog.xlsx'/'Full Backlog'. The workbook is HAND-maintained (consistent with the banner being hand-patched while the body rotted), and CLAUDE.md §7 lists 'regenerate backlog.xlsx' as a manual sprint-close step that is routinely skipped (BACKLOG.md flags 'needs regen' 4x). git mtime pins the snapshot to 2026-06-02 02:46, before the 2026-06-03 work.

RECOMMENDATION — RETIRE (both-agree, with a conditional). Drop backlog.xlsx from tracking and rely on BACKLOG.md as the single source of truth; this removes a perennial drift source and the tracked-binary churn. Regenerating is NOT a config change — because no generator exists, 'keep-and-regenerate' requires WRITING a BACKLOG.md→xlsx generator first (real net-new work for a view nobody consumes — the Dashboard has never even been recalculated). So: RETIRE unless a stakeholder specifically needs a spreadsheet/Dashboard view, in which case build the generator (parses BACKLOG.md, writes the 4 canonical status strings, recalc-on-save, fixes the gate sheets, re-sorts by ID incl. the SIM-403b 'b'-suffix) and run+verify it as a hard sprint-close step before re-keeping. Either way, when xlsx and BACKLOG.md disagree, BACKLOG.md wins. Housekeeping: gitignore/remove the untracked xlsx_fullbacklog.json scratch dump and add a '~$*' .gitignore pattern for Excel lock files.
